full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-1-2006 (decree signed on 24-1-2006), passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No.40 of 2005, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 10-5-2005 (decree signed on 12-5-2005), passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Baliakandi, Rajbari, in Title Suit No.16 of 2006, should not be set-aside, and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. The Trial Court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the oral and documentary evidences on record, dismissed the suit by her judgment and decree dated 10-5-2005 (decree signed on 12-5-2005). 

 5. Against the said judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs-Appellants-Opposite Parties preferred Title Appeal No.40 of 2005 before the District Judge, Rajbari, which was heard by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajbari, who, being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and decree, allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court dated 17-1-2006 (decree signed on 24-1-2006). 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the defendant-Respondent No. 1-Petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. Learned Advocates Mr Naim Ahmed and Mr Khandaker Shahriar Shakir appeared for the petitioner. Mr Shakir, having placed the petition, judgments of both the courts below, the evidence adduced by the parties and other materials on record, first of all submits that, the admitted position is that, Md Majed Mridha was the owner of the suit property. The plaintiffs further case is that, Md Majed Mridha died leaving his 2(two) sons, one daughter and his 2nd wife i.e. the petitioner Tara Bibi (defendant No. 1), as his heirs in the suit property. On the contrary, he next points out that, the defendant's plain case is that the plaintiffs and the defendant are neither in joint possession, nor are they co-sharers by inheritance in the suit property. Rather, by a registered deed No. 999 dated 8-3-1997, the defendant-petitioner Tara Bibi has purchased the suit property from Md Majed Mridha (her husband and father of the plaintiffs). He then submits that, the trial court has framed proper issues and meticulously discussed the evidence on record and has come to a correct finding that, before his death, Md Majzed Mridha had transferred the suit property, vide deed No. 999 dated 08.03.1997 (Ext. Kha) to his 2nd wife, the defendant No. 1 Tara Bibi. He further submits that, although the plaintiffs had managed to produce the attesting witness Bashiram Das, as PW 2, to support their case, however, the trial court has compared the signature of the said witness Bashiram Das, that he had put on the kabala deed No. 999 dated 8-3-1997 (Ext. Kha), with his admitted signature made in another deed No. 4788 dated 5-11-1995, in which, the said Bashiram Das and his wife Sreemoti Kalitara Das were the sellers/executants. He proceeds on that, the trial court, after comparison of these signatures, has rightly arrived at the finding that, the signature put on the deed No. 999 dated 8-3-1997 (Ext. Kha) was that of the attesting witness Bashiram Das. The learned Advocate further submits that, the DW 2 Moslem Biswas, who is maternal uncle of the plaintiff, has admitted that he was present at the time of writing the deed No. 999 dated 8-3-1997 (Ext. Kha) and that the attesting witness Bashiram Das has put his signature on the said deed in his presence. He next pointed out that, Bashiram Das (PW 2) has also put his signature below the affidavit annexed to the said deed, as required by PO 92 of 1972. Therefore, the trial court has rightly arrived at the finding that, since Md Majed Mridha has transferred the title and possession of the suit property, vide deed No. 999 dated 8-3-1997, in favour of the defendant No. 1 Tara Bibi, therefore he left nothing in the suit property (schedule Kha) to be inherited by two sons and one daughter of the deceased Md Majed Mridha. But, the appellate court has not properly assessed the evidence on record placed before it and, as such, it has wrongly reversed the judgment of the trial court. Therefore, he concludes that, the appellate court has committed grave error of law, resulting in error in the impugned decision, occasioning failure of justice. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside, and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court may kindly be upheld. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr Md Khurshid Alain Khan appeared on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1-3. Mr Khan submits that, admittedly the suit property belonged to Md Majed Mridha, who died leaving the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 1 Tara Bibi, his 2nd wife, as his heirs. He further submits that, there was no reason for Md Majed Mridha to transfer the suit property to his 2nd wife, as alleged, by depriving his two sons and one daughter. He also submits that, the entire case of the defendant No. 1 is concocted and the transfer was not done for any consideration. The PW 2 has also testified that he did not sign the impugned deed as the attesting witness, he also submits. But, the trial court has failed to find that there was no consideration for the alleged impugned sale to the defendant No. 1, nor the execution of the deed has been properly proved. Hence, the finding of the trial court is based on no evidence. He next argues that, the appellate court has rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree by setting aside the judgment of the trial court, upon proper appreciation of evidence on record and that, this Rule has no merit and the same is liable to be discharged. 

 21. Hence, I am of the opinion that, the appellate court has misread the evidence on record and has committed grave error of law that has resulted in error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside, his findings be reversed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court should be upheld. 

 The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-1-2006 (decree signed on 24-1-2006), passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No.40 of 2005, is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 10-5-2005 (decree signed on 12-5-2005), passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Baliakandi, Rajbari, in Title Suit No.16 of 2006 is hereby affirmed.
